name: vllm
description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
one_liner: Software that runs large AI language models efficiently on your own servers, instead of paying a cloud AI provider per request.
buyer: A law firm or healthcare provider's IT lead who needs an AI chat assistant but is contractually or legally barred from sending client data to an external AI vendor.
business_use_cases: A law firm self-hosts an open-weight model behind it to get an internal AI chat assistant where client data never leaves their own servers.
A healthcare company builds a HIPAA-conscious internal AI tool on top of it instead of relying on a third-party API with uncertain data handling.
A GPU-cloud reseller offers 'private LLM inference' as a service built on it, for customers who need self-hosted AI but don't want to run the infrastructure themselves.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a 'private, self-hosted AI chat' setup and support package for regulated-industry clients (law, health, finance).
Run a managed private-inference hosting service and charge per-GPU-hour or per-seat.

steal_this: Stand up a self-hosted chat assistant on one open-weight model this weekend, wire it into a document search tool, and pitch it to one local law or accounting firm as 'ChatGPT that never leaves your building.'
